Bash manual, Lists of Commands: "If a command is terminated by the control operator '&', the shell executes the command asynchronously in a subshell." So an unquoted & ends the curl command there and the rest (offset=2) is parsed as a separate command.

Section 3 now reads "a `name=value` pair after the `?` in a URL, such as `limit=20`, that the server reads as an option for the request; here the path still points at the product collection". No longer contradicts RFC 9110 4.2.1 ("The hierarchical path component and optional query component identify the target resource"). model-binding.md: "Looks through the sources and finds \"DogsOnly=true\" in the query string." Lab: ?limit=3&offset=2 binds both by name (ids 3,4,5). Old section-4 sentence removed.

Design reasoning, not version-dependent behaviour. Consistent with the code: without Take/Skip the SQL has no LIMIT, so every row is read, projected and serialized server-side before any response byte reaches the client.

claim_verdicts.evidence: Stated with its condition ("so the client learns its request was wrong"), and the lesson describes what Đơn Hàng does rather than prescribing it universally. The behaviour half (refuse, not clamp) is verified under claim 7.

PG17 7.6: "OFFSET says to skip that many rows before beginning to return rows." 13.2.1: a SELECT "sees only data committed before the query began"; "two successive SELECT commands can see different data ... if other transactions commit changes after the first SELECT starts and before the second SELECT starts." Each page request is a new SELECT, so positions are counted on the data at that moment; an insert/delete before the offset shifts later rows. Docs opened R3: both pages.
